The bullish narrative saw a fair value of US$6.54, built on the idea that Recursion OS 2.0 and tools like Boltz-2 could make drug discovery faster and more cost effective, with analysts assuming revenue growth of 50.7% a year.

The bearish view pointed to a fair value of US$3, highlighting high research spend, early stage programs and regulatory risk, with its assumptions using a slower 16.5% annual revenue growth rate.

What The Results Changed For Recursion Pharmaceuticals

The most telling update for Recursion Pharmaceuticals was that Q3 2026 revenue reached US$18.6 million, compared with US$5.2 million a year earlier. This supported the bullish focus on commercial traction and partnerships. Net loss also narrowed from US$162.3 million to US$119.0 million, yet the business still reported a loss, so profitability in the optimistic story remained unproven. Overall, the evidence cut both ways.

The lesson is simple. When a growth story leans on future operating leverage, check whether losses are shrinking in absolute terms alongside higher sales, not just whether headline revenue moved.

What You Would Be Paying For Today With Recursion Pharmaceuticals
